source_text: No explicit geometry described; assume downward triangle representing Shakti.

The Dakṣiṇāmūrti Saṃhitā describes the yantra as a triangle, hexagon, 16 petals, eight petals, then bhūpurahttps://shivashakti.com/nitya#:~:text=The%20DS%20describes%20her%20yantra,The%20vidy%C4%81%20mantra%20also%20differs.

The Dakṣiṇāmūrti Saṃhitā describes her yantra as a trikona (triangle) with eight petals and an earth square (bhūpura)https://shivashakti.com/nitya#:~:text=The%20Dak%E1%B9%A3i%E1%B9%87am%C5%ABrti%20Samhita%20

The Dakṣiṇāmūrti Saṃhitā describes her yantra as a triangle, eight petals and bhūpura; the triangle contains the deities Shikhini, Nilakanthi and Raudrihttps://shivashakti.com/nitya#:~:text=The%20DS%20describes%20her%20yantra,The%20vidy%C4%81%20mantra%20also%20differs.
Her yantra has eight trikonas (triangles) and twelve petals representing the 12 zodiac signshttps://shivashakti.com/nitya#:~:text=Vahnivasini%20is%20the%20fifth%20Nity%C4%81

The Dakṣiṇāmūrti Saṃhitā describes her yantra as consisting of a triangle, four petals, eight petals and a bhūpurahttps://shivashakti.com/nitya#:~:text=The%20description%20in%20the%20DS,eight%20petals%20and%20a%20bh%C5%ABpura.
No explicit yantra geometry is given for Śivadūtī; based on patterns, assume a downward triangle with eight petals and bhūpura.
Tvaritā’s yantra has eight petals containing eight Śaktīshttps://shivashakti.com/nitya#:~:text=Her%20%C5%9Aakt%C4%ABs%20are%20Humkari%2C%20Khechari%2C
Geometry not specified; assume downward triangle with eight petals and bhūpura to maintain pattern.
Geometry not provided in sources; assign pattern of downward triangle with twelve petals (double lotus).
Tantrarāja describes Nilapatākā as sapphire-hued but doesn’t specify her yantra; we assume a downward triangle with eight petals and bhūpura.
Vijayā’s mantra and dhyāna are described but the yantra is not; assign typical pattern of downward triangle with eight petals and bhūpura.
Sarvamaṅgalā is described with a lotus yantra but geometry details are absent; assume a downward triangle with eight petals and bhūpura.
Dakṣiṇāmūrti Saṃhitā notes that one of her mandalas has 32 petals and another variant has 40 petalshttps://shivashakti.com/nitya#:~:text=The%20DS%20gives%20a%20different
Citrā is described in the Tantrarāja but her yantra details are scarce; assign a downward triangle with 16 petals to align with the lunar cycle.
